questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the most common shortcut that leaves a security document unable to answer whether a specific user can see a specific sensitive field?
options: Documenting only the organization-wide default setting and calling the security documentation done, without covering sharing rules, permission sets, and field-level security together
Documenting only field-level security and skipping every other layer
Including an access matrix instead of prose
Writing the document before the org is built
questions.explain: Answering 'can this user see this data' depends on all six layers combined (OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, manual/Apex sharing, permission sets/profiles, field-level security) — stopping at OWD alone leaves that question unanswerable.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend an access matrix as the primary artifact for communicating a sharing model?
options: Because it replaces the need to configure OWD at all
Because it answers 'can this role see this data' in one glance, after all sharing layers are already combined, rather than forcing the reader to mentally combine six layers of prose themselves
Because Salesforce requires an access matrix before deployment
Because it shows the exact Apex trigger order of execution
questions.explain: The access matrix format pre-combines the effect of all the sharing layers into a single table of role/profile by object/field, so a reader gets the practical answer directly instead of deriving it from separate layer-by-layer descriptions.

questions.q: In the order this lesson lists them, which sharing-model layer is evaluated first, forming the baseline before anything else opens access back up?
options: Field-level security
Permission sets and profiles
Organization-wide defaults (OWD)
Manual and Apex-managed sharing
questions.explain: Organization-wide defaults set the baseline record-level access (Private, Public Read Only, or Public Read/Write) before role hierarchy, sharing rules, manual/Apex sharing, permission sets, and field-level security apply on top of it.

questions.q: In this lesson's Opportunity OWD example, why does the document state the reasoning ('Private, not Public Read Only, specifically so the Finance sharing rule is the only path to broad visibility') rather than just the setting itself?
options: Because stating reasoning is required by Salesforce's terms of service
Because Private OWD cannot function unless its justification is documented in the same object
Because Finance sharing rules only work if OWD is Public Read Only

Because without the reasoning, a future admin might 'fix' what looks like an overly restrictive OWD setting without realizing a downstream sharing rule depends on that baseline, risking an accidental, ungoverned access change
questions.explain: A setting without reasoning invites exactly the kind of accidental, risky change this lesson warns about — documenting why Private OWD matters here makes the Finance rule's role as the single auditable path to broad access clear, rather than leaving that intent invisible.

questions.q: Which layer can restrict a user's access to a specific piece of data even when that user already has full object and record-level access to the parent record?
options: Field-level security
Organization-wide defaults
Role hierarchy
Sharing rules
questions.explain: Field-level security is the final layer this lesson lists — it can restrict visibility or editability of a specific field even when a user otherwise has full object and record access, which is why the access matrix example includes a sensitive field as its own column.
